title: Podman does not honor users from libnss
body:
### Issue Description

When trying to run a container with the option `--userns keep-id` as a user that does not exist in `/etc/passwd`, the command fails.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Setup NSS as user backend (e.g. LDAP).
2. Install rootless podman and add mappings in `/etc/subuid` and `/etc/subgid`.
3. Try to run a container with the `--userns keep-id` option.


### Describe the results you received

```
$ podman run --userns keep-id alpine:latest cat /etc/os-release
Error: creating temporary passwd file for container f6a32fdc64804a031c68793153272738f6bafcb092e5591232d64f1961831ba6: failed to get current user: user: lookup userid 12000: operation not permitted
```

The user does exist

```
$ getent passwd <username>
<username>:x:12000:12000:<name>,,,,<uuid>:/home/<username>:/bin/bash
```

but it is not stored in `/etc/passwd`.

### Describe the results you expected

Without the option, it works fine:

```
$ podman run alpine:latest cat /etc/os-release
NAME="Alpine Linux"
ID=alpine
VERSION_ID=3.24.1
...
```

comments.body:
> operation not permitted

That suggest podman likely does correctly use libnsss as configured but your implementation returns EPERM as erro on the user lookup.
Mostly likely it cannot deal with the user namespace podman runs usner, what happens if you run `podman unshare getent passwd $(id -u)`?

The --userns keep-id option maps your current user into the container so it has to lookup the current user for that in order to add that into the containers /etc/passwd.
